name: Jesse
description: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy

points: Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it; and the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

note.label: Ruth 4: Boaz Redeems the Inheritance

points: Samuel is told to fill his horn with oil and go to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for the Most High had already provided himself a king from among Jesse's sons.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Samuel answered peaceably: he came to sacrifice to the Lord, and he sanctified Jesse and his sons and called them to the sacrifice.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, the older, bigger, more developed ones, and Samuel said of each, Neither hath the Lord chosen this; the Lord had not chosen any of these.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Asked whether these were all his children, Jesse answered that there remained yet the youngest, and behold, he keepeth the sheep. Samuel would not sit down until the young one was fetched. He was ruddy, of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to, a young handsome fella, and the Most High said, Arise, anoint him, for this is he.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: One of the servants had seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite that is cunning in playing, a mighty valiant man, a man of war, prudent in matters, a comely person, and the Lord is with him. He did not say the name, but this son of Jesse who went hard on the instruments was David.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Saul sent to Jesse: send me David thy son, which is with the sheep. Jesse sent David with bread, a bottle of wine, and a kid, and David came to Saul, stood before him, and Saul loved him greatly.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Saul asked Jesse to let David stand before him, for he hath found favour in my sight; Saul liked the spirit on that young brother, and every king keeps a young soldier always with him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehemjudah named Jesse, who had eight sons. The three eldest, Eliab, Abinadab, and Shammah, followed Saul to the battle; the same three the Most High refused in chapter 16.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: Jesse sent David to the camp with parched corn and ten loaves for his brethren and ten cheeses for their captain of the thousand, to see how his brethren fared and take their pledge.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: And Saul said to him, Whose son art thou, thou young man? And David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: That first day Saul spake not anything, for he thought something had befallen David, that surely he was not clean; but on the second day of the month, with David's place empty again, Saul asked Jonathan, Wherefore cometh not the son of Jesse to meat?

note.label: 1 Samuel 20: David's Empty Seat at the New Moon

points: Saul got wind that his own son was hiding David out. When Jonathan covered for David, Saul's anger was kindled against Jonathan: as long as the son of Jesse liveth upon the ground, thou shalt not be established, nor thy kingdom.

note.label: 1 Samuel 20: David's Empty Seat at the New Moon

points: Nabal answered, Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse? there be many servants now a days that break away every man from his master. He was talking much smack, as if he did not even know who David was, and refused to give of his bread, his water, and his flesh to men he knew not.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

points: These are the last words of David, the son of Jesse, the man raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob and the sweet psalmist of Israel. The spirit of the Lord spoke by him and his word was in David's tongue; this shows David was a prophet, and the book of Psalms are songs of prophecy. The God of Israel, the rock of Israel, spoke to him.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel.

note.label: Abya Yala Under Fire

points: The spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the captains, who said, "Thine are we, David, and on thy side, thou son of Jesse: peace be unto thee, for thy God helpeth thee." David received them and made them captains.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

points: When all Israel sees the king will not listen, they answer that they have no portion in David nor inheritance in the son of Jesse, and every man departs to his tent.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended.

note.label: Psalm 72: All Nations Shall Serve Him

points: And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots. Who is that stem that is going to come out of Jesse?

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse: Christ. The Messiah is the branch that shall grow out of his roots. And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.

note.label: Perilous Times: Judges and Soldiers

points: There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots. This is a prophecy of Christ. The Spirit of the Most High rests upon Him: wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and the fear of the Most High.

note.label: Isaiah 11: The Rod of Jesse and the Second Gathering

points: The root of Jesse is Christ, the ensign the people look to, and the Gentiles who seek to it in verse 10 are the remnant of his people in verse 11.

note.label: The Art of War - Rules of Engagement

points: In that day there shall be a root of Jesse: that is Christ, the ensign. To it shall the Gentiles seek, and his rest shall be glorious. Read the context before you make the Gentiles here the heathen nations: the ones who need rest are the ones in captivity.

note.label: The Religious Peer Pressure of Fred Price Jr

points: In that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek. So Christ is that ensign, and the Gentiles shall seek to Christ. This is a good scripture to explain Gentiles in conjunction with Matthew 4:15.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: In that day there shall be a root of Jesse standing for an ensign of the people; Jesse refers to Christ, and to Him the Gentiles shall seek, and His rest shall be glorious.

note.label: Isaiah 11: The Rod of Jesse and the Second Gathering

points: Generation goes back to genes and genealogy: Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar, Phares begat Esrom, down to Naasson, Salmon, Booz of Rachab, Obed of Ruth, Jesse and David the king.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: To whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart. So what is the caveat to being sovereign, to being a ruler, and to being over God's heritage? A man after mine own heart. After exactly how the Lord wanted his servants to be, a king to be, is exactly what David was.

note.label: Sovereign Idiocracy
